Context Agenda 2063 is Africa’s long-term development blueprint for achieving “The Africa We Want.” As the continent is in the Decade of Acceleration, there is increasing recognition that delivering Agenda 2063 requires more than awareness of continental aspirations and policy frameworks. It requires citizens, institutions, young people, communities, businesses, and leaders to position themselves as active contributors within systems that create value, solve problems, and sustain progress over time. The “Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces” traineeship was established to support this shift - from awareness to contribution, from inspiration to execution, and from participation to stewardship. The first cohort of the initiative attracted more than 600 participants from across the world and generated important lessons regarding engagement, delivery systems, accountability, and the need to position Agenda 2063 not only as a policy framework, but also as a multi-market platform through which Africans can contribute to building the Africa We Want. Building on these lessons, the second cohort will engage 500 Online Volunteers through a structured 7-week traineeship combined with a longer-term engagement model. The traineeship will support participants to define their contribution across the decades leading to 2063, identify the values and routines that will sustain their journey, and develop practical pathways for action within their respective power spaces. The traineeship also seeks to strengthen a growing continental network of young people and practitioners committed to long-term transformation, collaboration, and delivery of Agenda 2063 aspirations and related Moonshots. At the end of the traineeship, participants will produce a “Letter from the Future” dated 30 January 2063, reflecting on the Africa that was realized and the role they played in shaping it. title: Routine Data Quality Audit (RDQAs) Consultant – Ethiopia (Addis Ababa & Hawassa) – 2026
description: Ethiopia Routine Data Quality Audit (RDQAs) Consultant – Ethiopia (Addis Ababa & Hawassa) – 2026 Organization Tiko Posted 11 May 2026 Closing date 20 May 2026 Tiko Africa is a non-profit organisation founded in 2014, dedicated to empowering adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) aged 15–24 in low-income communities. Our work focuses on improving the sexual and reproductive health (SRH) of AGYW in Sub-Saharan Africa, addressing the “Triple Threat” of early pregnancy, HIV, and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). In Ethiopia, Tiko partners with private franchised and non-franchised health facilities, public health facilities, and local government authorities (AACAHB and Hawassa City Health Department (HCHD)). Through these partnerships, Tiko ensures AGYW have access to high-quality HIV, SRH, SGBV, and mental health services supported by high-quality and verifiable data. Tiko Africa seeks a qualified consultant to conduct routine, systematic Data Quality Audits (RDQAs) and facilitate Strategic Data Review Sessions at Tiko-supported health facilities in Addis Ababa and Hawassa. Scope of Work Coordination and Joint DQA Participation: Working closely with Tiko, the consultant will support coordination with local government authorities (AACAHB, HCHD, and respective Sub-City Health Offices) to facilitate and participate in joint on-site RDQA activities. On-Site RDQA Execution: Conduct full on-site RDQA processes, including data extraction, tallying, and comparative verification between services reported on the Tiko platform and official primary source registers (HMIS). Document key process observations, facility capacity gaps, and the condition of health records at facilities visited. The RDQA must also include documentation of broader contextual factors (e.g., donor funding shifts or new health policies) that could impact data quality or service delivery. Root Cause Analysis and Action Planning: Identify the root causes of discrepancies (e.g., staff attitude, stock-outs, misunderstanding of the Tiko app, transcription errors, or intentional data falsification). Findings must be triangulated, and corrective action points must be developed collaboratively with facility staff. Reporting: Submit compiled raw data and clean datasets, along with a detailed Comparative Checks Report documenting all variances, root causes, and recommended corrective actions. Follow-Up: Conduct structured post-RDQA follow-ups to ensure all action points have been addressed before the next audit cycle. Support for Facility Data Review Sessions: Support Tiko in executing quarterly Facility Data Review Sessions involving facility in-charges, providers, data personnel, Health Extension Workers (HEWs), and Tiko staff. The consultant will present performance trends, demand generation trends, and Quality Assurance (QA) findings, linking data discrepancies to Facility Improvement Plans (FIP). Objectives of the Routine Data Quality Audits (RDQAs) Verify the accuracy of reported data against national HMIS tools and data. Identify gaps and drive continuous performance improvements. Ensure that previous action points are fully addressed before the next audit cycle. Methodology Quantitative verification of registers and service counts using RDQA tools. Data triangulation across: Tiko Platform Data Facility Source Documents (Primary Registers) National Health Information System (DHIS2) Qualitative root cause analysis interviews. Follow-up and gap closure activities. Participatory Facility Data Review Sessions.
